### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU (Intel/AMD)
• Motherboard (socket, chipset, form‑factor)
• RAM (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity)
• GPU (if not integrated)
• Storage (SSD/HDD, NVMe or SATA)
• Power Supply Unit (PSU, wattage, 80+ rating)
• Case (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX, size, airflow)
• Cooling (stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, AIO liquid cooler)
• Operating System (Windows, Linux, etc.) | Check compatibility lists (e.g., CPU‑to‑Motherboard socket, PSU wattage). | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat, static‑free surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap or anti‑static mat.
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Avoid carpeted floors; static can damage components. | | 4 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the motherboard’s CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket.
• Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount on the CPU.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | For AIO coolers, attach the pump to the motherboard header. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch with the slot and press until the clips click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard in the Case** | • Align standoffs with motherboard holes.
• Screw the motherboard onto the standoffs. | Use the correct screw length; avoid overtightening. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot.
• Secure with screws or retention clips. | For NVMe, align the notch and push until it clicks. | | 9 | **Install the Power Supply** | • Place PSU in the case’s PSU tray.
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables to the motherboard, GPU, drives, and case fans. | Keep cables tidy; use cable ties or Velcro straps. | | 10 | **Connect Motherboard Power** | • 24‑pin ATX power connector.
• 8‑pin (or 4‑pin) CPU power connector. | Double‑check orientation; connectors are keyed. | | 11 | **Install GPU (if applicable)** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers from the case.
• Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws. | Connect required PCI‑e power cables from PSU. | | 12 | **Connect Peripheral Cables** | • Front panel connectors (power button, reset, USB, audio).
• Case fans (PWM or 3‑pin).
• Any additional headers (RGB, SATA power). | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | | 13 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
• Use cable ties or Velcro straps. | Good airflow and easier future upgrades. | | 14 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Power on.
• Enter BIOS (usually DEL or F2).
• Check that CPU, RAM, storage are detected. | Update BIOS if needed (download latest firmware from motherboard site). | | 15 | **Install Operating System** | • Create bootable USB (Windows Media Creation Tool, Rufus, or Linux ISO).
• Boot from USB and follow installation prompts. | Install drivers after OS is up (chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi). | | 16 | **Install Drivers & Software** | • GPU drivers (NVIDIA/AMD).
• Chipset drivers.
• Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth drivers.
• Update Windows or Linux kernel. | Keep system updated for security and performance. | | 17 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits (<80 °C for CPU, <85 °C for GPU). | | 18 | **Final Adjustments** | • Add additional fans or RGB lighting.
• Install any extra storage or expansion cards.
• Clean dust filters. | Keep the system well‑ventilated. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU installed - [ ] GPU installed (if needed) - [ ] Storage installed - [ ] All power cables connected - [ ] Front panel connectors attached - [ ] First boot successful - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers updated - [ ] Benchmarked & temperatures checked --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | PC won’t power on | PSU not connected or switched off | Verify PSU switch, check all power cables | | No display | GPU not seated or wrong power connector | Re‑seat GPU, connect PCI‑e power | | Overheating | Poor airflow, inadequate cooling | Add case fans, improve cable management | | BIOS not detecting RAM | Incorrect slot or incompatible RAM | Try different slots, check compatibility | | Windows install fails | Corrupt USB, wrong partition scheme | Re‑create USB, use GPT for UEFI | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – component compatibility checker, price comparison. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware for visual guides. - **Manuals** – always keep motherboard, PSU, and case manuals handy (PDFs on manufacturer sites). Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know the specific issue and I can help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
